title: Identification of MEOX1 as a potential target in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver fibrosis.
authors: Jiao, Xiaoxiao; Lai, Linying; Qian, Yiting; Sun, Bo; Yang, Wenzhuo
journal: The International journal of biological markers
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组与实验鉴定MASH肝纤维化中转录因子MEOX1及其靶点SERPINE1，并用AlphaFold/PyMOL预测蛋白互作位点，虽涉及TF-DNA调控但核心为疾病机制与靶点发现，方法上仅简单结构预测，深度不足。
abstract: BackgroundThe mechanisms underlying the occurrence and progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)-related liver fibrosis remains poorly understood. This study aims to identify key transcription factors involved in the development of liver fibrosis in MASH patients, thereby providing potential targets for drug discovery.MethodsMicroarray data were retrieved from liver biopsy specimens of MASH patients exhibiting varying stages of fibrosis via the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Differentially expressed transcription factors (DETFs) were identified through the application of Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis. A set of in vitro and in vivo experiments were conducted to investigate the role of MEOX1 in MASH-related fibrosis. To delineate the potential mechanisms, the transcriptomic RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), Alphafold, and PyMOL were used.ResultsA total of six DETFs (MEOX1, SOX4, LEF1, SOX9, MYC, and CBX2) were identified as being positively correlated with the progression of MASH-related fibrosis. MEOX1 was increased in mouse model of MASH diet-induced liver fibrosis and hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) stimulated by transforming growth factor-beta1. Knockdown of the MEOX1 markedly suppressed the activation, proliferation, and migration of HSCs. RNA-Seq analysis identified serine protease inhibitor family E member 1 (SERPINE1) as the critical target of MEOX1 within HSCs. The protein interaction sites of MEOX1 and SERPINE1 were predicted using Alphafold and PyMOL.ConclusionIn summary, as a pivotal transcription factor, MEOX1 activates HSCs via SERPINE1, thereby promoting liver fibrosis associated with MASH. Inhibition of the MEOX1-SERPINE1 pathway could offer a novel therapeutic avenue for treating MASH-related fibrosis.
abstract_zh: 背景代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎（MASH）相关肝纤维化的发生和进展机制仍知之甚少。本研究旨在识别参与MASH患者肝纤维化发展的关键转录因子，从而为药物发现提供潜在靶点。方法通过基因表达综合（Gene Expression Omnibus）数据库获取来自不同纤维化分期MASH患者肝活检标本的微阵列数据。应用加权基因共表达网络分析（Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis）鉴定差异表达转录因子（DETFs）。进行一系列体外和体内实验以探究MEOX1在MASH相关纤维化中的作用。为描绘潜在机制，使用了转录组RNA测序（RNA-seq）、Alphafold和PyMOL。结果共鉴定出六个DETFs（MEOX1、SOX4、LEF1、SOX9、MYC和CBX2）与MASH相关纤维化进展呈正相关。在MASH饮食诱导的肝纤维化小鼠模型及转化生长因子-β1刺激的肝星状细胞（HSCs）中，MEOX1表达升高。敲低MEOX1显著抑制了HSCs的活化、增殖和迁移。RNA-Seq分析确定丝氨酸蛋白酶抑制剂家族E成员1（SERPINE1）为HSCs中MEOX1的关键靶点。使用Alphafold和PyMOL预测了MEOX1与SERPINE1的蛋白相互作用位点。结论总之，作为关键转录因子，MEOX1通过SERPINE1激活HSCs，从而促进MASH相关肝纤维化。抑制MEOX1-SERPINE1通路可能为治疗MASH相关纤维化提供新的治疗途径。
